the-apprentice-2024.gazette: Roy Cohn left the McCarthy hearings with a client list and a method: attack, deny everything, never concede. The film works from what survived on paper — the 1973 federal housing-discrimination suit against the family company, Cohn's documented tactics, and Ivana Trump's sworn divorce deposition. Testimony given in a matrimonial court forty years ago is now the primary source for a feature film.

the-order-2024.gazette: Between 1983 and 1984 a splinter cell calling itself the Brüder Schweigen ran counterfeiting, armed robbery, and murder across the Pacific Northwest to bankroll a war it believed had already started. Denver radio host Alan Berg was shot in his driveway in June 1984; the FBI manhunt ended that December in a burning house on Whidbey Island. The reporting collected in The Silent Brotherhood remains the picture's spine.

april-2025.gazette: Kulumbegashvili films in long static takes and holds them well past the point of comfort. The camera stays put in rural Georgian rooms and on roadsides while a scene runs its full length, refusing the cuts that normally spare a viewer the middle of things. That fixity is the film's contract: what happens in front of the lens is shown for as long as it takes.
april-2025.prism: A shot that never cuts leaves nobody the excuse of having missed it. The cost is endurance — the film asks for it up front and settles accounts much later.

blue-moon-2025.gazette: On March 31, 1943, Oklahoma! opened at the St. James Theatre and reset the terms of the American musical inside a single evening. Lorenz Hart spent the night at Sardi's while his former partner's new collaboration turned into the biggest thing on Broadway. Hart was dead by November.

caught-by-the-tides-2025.gazette: Jia Zhangke started rolling in 2001 and never entirely stopped, accumulating footage of Datong, the Yangtze towns, and whatever crowd stood in front of the lens that year. The Three Gorges resettlement emptied those towns, SARS shut them, and the pandemic sealed them again two decades on. Because the film is cut from the accumulation itself, the aging on screen is actual elapsed time.

it-was-just-an-accident-2025.gazette: Jafar Panahi has been under an official filmmaking ban in Iran since 2010. This one was shot regardless: no permits, no sanctioned production, cast and crew working outside state approval. The realism here is not a stylistic preference but the physical condition of the shoot.
it-was-just-an-accident-2025.prism: A film made without permission runs up a bill that comes due after the credits, and the people who signed on are not all as shielded as the director. Clandestine production is a method, but it's also a risk distributed very unevenly across a crew.

nouvelle-vague-2025.gazette: Breathless was shot around Paris in the late summer of 1959 on almost no money, financed by Georges de Beauregard off the strength of a Truffaut treatment. Raoul Coutard worked handheld and from a wheelchair pushed along the pavement; the jump cuts came later, in the edit, when the picture had to shed running time. Linklater reconstructs those weeks in black and white, down to the improvisation and the shortages that a year later were being called a movement's house style.

roofman-2025.gazette: Jeffrey Manchester's method was the roof: cut a hole, drop in before opening, empty the safe, apologize to the staff on the way out. After escaping a North Carolina prison in 2004 he moved into a Charlotte Toys 'R' Us, living behind a false wall in the stockroom and eating off the shelves. The arrangement held for roughly six months before the arrest came in early 2005.

the-smashing-machine-2025.gazette: Mark Kerr competed in the years before unified rules and state commissions — open-weight tournaments in Brazil, arena cards in Japan, a sport still arguing about what it was. John Hyams followed him with a camera for the 2002 documentary that supplies this film its title and much of its material, painkillers and overdose included. The record and the damage accumulated across the same few short years.
the-smashing-machine-2025.prism: The source documentary is still out there, so this is a restaging of a life already on tape, and the new thing being sold is the transformation rather than the story. The unregulated era that made Kerr a draw is also the one that left nobody accountable for what it ran up.
